recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-5328 unless Patient Care later decides to add separate lifecycle-status timing in addition to the current achievement-status date.
issue_request: FHIR-5328 is a Published/Persuasive Patient Care ballot comment for FHIR-core Goal asking for timing on goals: when a goal was met and when it is expected to be met. The recorded resolution was to add a status date and a target date to achieve the goal.
initial_application: No prior combined-branch audit commit existed for FHIR-5328. The apparent original application is git commit db4ace37c6615c9732f958d34d6286fe739fc657, a 2015 PC-approved Goal rewrite that added Goal.targetDate and Goal.statusDate to the historical Goal spreadsheet.
additional_context: Goal is active in the current build through source/fhir.ini. The old Goal.targetDate concept is now Goal.target.due[x]. The old Goal.statusDate was later clarified by FHIR-53981 and renamed to Goal.achievementStatusDate. FHIR-9084 later requested dateTime precision for Goal dates but was withdrawn/resolved no-change.
reconciliation: No source change was needed. source/goal/structuredefinition-Goal.xml defines Goal.achievementStatusDate and Goal.target.due[x], the Goal target-date search parameter is present, and the example uses both achievementStatusDate and dueDate.

related_jiras.note: Later Applied R6 issue that renamed Goal.statusDate to Goal.achievementStatusDate and clarified that the date applies to achievement status.
Later Resolved - No Change / Retracted request to make Goal dates dateTime, supporting that current date precision is intentional.
